## Summary

A driven child's `implement.py finish` is refused when the pre-push full-suite gate observes another live session's uncommitted edits in the **main checkout**. The gate reports `live_repo_mutation` ("the test suite changed a guarded checkout") and fails the run, so the push is refused — even though the child's own worktree is clean and its commit is composed only of its own files.

Observed while finishing WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR (tests-only, worktree clean, changed-scope green): the full-suite gate failed with

```
live-repo mutation detected: the test suite changed a guarded checkout for .../worktrees/wl-WL-0MWETWFSH...
  in main checkout /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub:
  added path [ M] docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-storage.ts
  added path [??] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.test.ts
  added path [??] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.ts
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts
```

Evidence that the mutation is concurrent agent activity, not the suite: `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.test.ts` has mtime 22:42:45, four seconds *after* the suite started at 22:42:41, and the paths belong to the host-dispatch-budget workstream (WL-0MWFJD1RV008FCCR, held by herdr-1794608223-1882173-11244, driving children from ~22:17). No test in this repo writes `.ts` sources.

## Why it matters

Any driven child finishing while any other session (or the operator) has the main checkout dirty will be blocked, and the report attributes the corruption to *this* child's worktree ("the test suite changed a guarded checkout") — so the natural next action is to hunt a bug in a clean tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gate distinguishes "changes pre-existing before the run / made by another live session" from "changes the suite made during this run" and only fails on the latter (compare against a start-of-run snapshot of the guarded checkout, not against `HEAD`)
- When it does fail, the report names the owning session/work item where one is discoverable (e.g. via `.implement_state.json` / claimed items) instead of implying the running item corrupted the tree
- A driven child whose own worktree is clean and whose changed-scope gate passed is not blocked by unrelated dirty paths in the main checkout
- Regression test covering: dirty main checkout, clean child worktree ⇒ gate passes; suite mutating the guarded checkout during the run ⇒ gate fails
- Full test suite passes

## Key Files

- skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py (live-repo mutation guard)
- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py (finish push gate)

## Impact

Agents stop chasing a phantom corruption bug when a concurrent session has the main checkout dirty, and driven children are no longer blocked by work they never touched.

## Summary

`implement.py finish` fast-forwards the local `dev` branch to the about-to-be-pushed tip **before** the push succeeds, and restores it on failure. A concurrent `implement.py start` that runs inside that window resolves `dev` to the unpushed commit and creates its worktree/branch from it — permanently grafting another item's commit onto the new branch.

Observed on 2026-11-13:

- WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR's finish created commit `e2291be45` (tests-only) and moved local `dev` to it before its push gate failed; finish then restored `dev` to `079948694`.
- `git reflog show wl-WL-0MWFJDGXQ001OXP8-append-only-audit-trail-for-budget-ledge` shows a single entry: `e2291be45 … branch: Created from dev` — i.e. the sibling child's worktree was created from the transient, unpushed tip.
- That branch is now `[ahead 1]` of `dev` with a foreign commit as its base, so its first push to `dev` will carry WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR's commit under the wrong item id (or dump both in one push).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `finish` never moves the local `dev` ref while a push is in flight; the post-push fast-forward happens only after `git push` reports success
- On a failed/refused push, local `dev` is provably unchanged from its pre-finish value (no write-then-restore window)
- `implement.py start` resolves its base from `origin/dev` (fetched) rather than a locally mutable `dev`, or refuses to branch from a `dev` that is not a known pushed tip
- Regression test: simulate a mid-push `start` and assert the new branch's base is the pushed tip, never an unpushed sibling commit
- Full test suite passes

## Key Files

- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py (finish push + dev sync; start base resolution)

## Impact

A new child's branch can no longer inherit another work item's unpushed commit, so each push to `dev` contains exactly the work item's own changes.
